newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine trade unions plan to call general strike.
newsitem.headline: Argentine trade unions plan to call general strike.

text.p: Argentina's labour confederation CGT said on Thursday night it would hold a general strike against economic policy and police repression.
It said it would announce a strike date on May 1.

"The government's ears are deaf to the demands of workers," CGT leader Rodolfo Daer told reporters. He also blasted businessmen whose "reactionary attitudes have caused the breakdown in three-way negotiations on labour reforms."
The strike would be the fourth staged since August, including two called against the government's free market labour reforms.

The strike announcement capped the CGT's self-styled "Day of National Mourning," during which workers walked off the job for one hour each shift to protest the death of a young woman in riots last weekend in the southern province of Neuquen.
Teresa Rodriguez, 24, died from a gunshot wound last Saturday when striking teachers and local residents clashed with paramilitary forces in the towns of Cutral-Co and Plaza Huincul in Neuquen.

Rodriguez, a mother of three children, was an innocent passer-by. Her death sparked a nationwide teachers strike Monday and a huge rally in the capital against the use of force to quell social unrest.
Neuquen teachers, who had been on strike for a month against 20 percent pay cuts, made a deal with provincial authorities this week to end the stoppage.

But a group of local residents has continued to block off access to national Highway 2, where the pitched battle with police took place last Saturday, demanding a solution to the region's high unemployment. The privatisation of oil giant YPF five years ago left thousands in the area jobless.
